title: Telco Admin Practice Quiz 3
note: Mixed NEC 2023 and theory. NEC references are approximate and should be verified against the actual Code book.

questions.question: which of the following is NOT a permissible wiring method specifically described as nonmetallic-sheathed cable under Article 334?
questions.explanation: Article 334 covers nonmetallic-sheathed cable types NM and NMC. Type SE (service-entrance) is covered in Article 338, so it is not an Article 334 NM cable wiring method.

questions.question: What is the maximum allowable ampacity for NM cable with 12 AWG copper conductors used for a residential branch circuit, as limited by the 2023 NEC?
questions.explanation: Section 240.4(D)(5) limits 12 AWG copper branch-circuit conductors to 20 A maximum. Section 334.80 also requires NM cable ampacity not to exceed the 60°C column in Table 310.16, which is 20 A for 12 AWG copper.

questions.question: Which of the following types of electrical boxes is NOT permitted for use in damp or wet locations?
choices: Metal box listed for wet locations
PVC box listed for wet locations
Fiberglass box listed for wet locations
questions.explanation: Article 314.15 requires boxes in damp or wet locations to be listed for that use. Standard listed boxes are metal or nonmetallic; a wooden box is not an acceptable listed wiring box for damp/wet locations.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable grounding electrode for a service entrance under the 2023 NEC?
choices: Metal underground water pipe in direct contact with earth for at least 10 feet
questions.explanation: Section 250.52(A) lists permitted grounding electrodes, including ground rods, metal underground water pipe with at least 10 ft in direct contact with earth, and concrete-encased electrodes. Nonconductive gas piping is not a grounding electrode and metal gas piping is explicitly prohibited as a grounding electrode in 250.52(B).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about electrical boxes and enclosures is correct?
choices: Electrical boxes must be securely fastened in place and be of sufficient strength to support fixtures.
Electrical boxes are not required to have covers if the wiring is properly terminated inside.
Junction boxes are allowed to be completely buried and inaccessible as long as they are marked on the plans.
There is no specific requirement for box fill calculations in the NEC.
questions.answer: Electrical boxes must be securely fastened in place and be of sufficient strength to support fixtures.
questions.explanation: Section 314.23 requires boxes to be securely fastened and supported. Sections 314.25, 314.16, and 314.29 also require covers, box fill calculations, and accessibility for junction boxes.

questions.question: What is the minimum size copper grounding electrode conductor required to connect to a rod or pipe electrode for a building or structure supplied by a 200-ampere service?
questions.explanation: Per 250.66(A), where the grounding electrode is a rod, pipe, or plate electrode, the grounding electrode conductor is not required to be larger than 6 AWG copper regardless of service ampacity.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable material for a standard electrical box or enclosure used in electrical installations?
questions.explanation: Article 314 permits electrical boxes of metal or nonmetallic material listed for the purpose. Common materials include steel, aluminum, and nonmetallic (like PVC). Copper is not used as the structural material for listed wiring boxes.

questions.question: What is the minimum size copper grounding electrode conductor required for a single ground rod used as the grounding electrode for a residential service?
questions.explanation: Section 250.66(A) states that the grounding electrode conductor to a rod, pipe, or plate electrode need not be larger than 6 AWG copper.

questions.question: In electrical terms, what does the acronym "GFCI" stand for?
questions.explanation: GFCI stands for Ground-Fault Circuit Interrupter, a device required by NEC 210.8 and other sections to protect personnel from ground-fault shock hazards.

questions.question: In practical residential wiring design, how many current-carrying conductors are typically allowed in a single NM cable before ampacity adjustment (derating) must be applied?
questions.explanation: When there are more than three current-carrying conductors in a cable or raceway, 310.15(C)(1) requires ampacity adjustment. Article 334.80 then limits NM cable to the 60°C ampacity after any adjustment, so three current-carrying conductors is the typical maximum before derating is required.

questions.question: What is the term used to describe the capacity of an electrical conductor to conduct current?
questions.explanation: Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance and describes how easily current flows through a conductor. It is a general electrical theory term rather than a specific NEC definition.

questions.question: What is the minimum size copper grounding electrode conductor required for a single rod or pipe electrode with a 200-ampere service?
questions.explanation: Again, 250.66(A) limits the grounding electrode conductor to a rod or pipe electrode to a maximum of 6 AWG copper, regardless of service size.

questions.question: What is the term used to describe the intentional connection of metallic objects together to ensure electrical continuity and conductivity?
questions.explanation: Article 100 defines Bonded (Bonding) as connected to establish electrical continuity and conductivity. Grounding is connection to earth; bonding is connection between conductive parts.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for electrical boxes and enclosures in typical NEC applications?
choices: Adequate space for the wiring and devices being used
Accessibility for inspection and maintenance (not permanently concealed)
Direct burial in soil without any protective covering
questions.answer: Direct burial in soil without any protective covering
questions.explanation: Boxes must be supported, provide adequate space, and remain accessible per Article 314. Direct burial of a standard box in soil without appropriate listing and protection is not an NEC requirement and would usually violate enclosure and corrosion protection rules.

questions.question: What is the maximum ampacity permitted for 14/2 NM cable with grounding used in residential branch-circuit wiring according to the 2023 NEC?
questions.explanation: Section 240.4(D)(3) limits 14 AWG copper branch-circuit conductors to 15 A maximum. Article 334.80 also requires NM to use the 60°C column of Table 310.16, where 14 AWG copper is 15 A.

questions.question: Which of the following conductor materials is NOT permitted to be used as a grounding electrode conductor?
choices: Aluminum in direct contact with earth or in wet locations
Galvanized steel wire that is part of a listed electrode
Copper-clad steel that is part of a listed electrode
questions.answer: Aluminum in direct contact with earth or in wet locations
questions.explanation: Article 250.62 and 250.64 prohibit the use of aluminum grounding electrode conductors where subject to corrosion, such as in direct contact with earth or in wet locations. Bare copper and listed steel or copper-clad steel components are permitted when used as part of listed grounding electrodes and installed per 250.52 and 250.68.
